changelog: Insert a fallback ordering that protects numeric expressions first: prefer cuts that keep a numeral/quantifier next to its immediately following unit/measurement (including %, currency, or parenthetic unit) over cuts that keep a finite verb with its immediate core complement, and prefer either of those over a punctuation/clause-boundary cut — this addresses the primary finding that numerals were being split while still providing a last-resort tie-breaker.
findings: The prompt treats numerals/quantities as safe cut points and therefore allows cuts that separate a numeral or quantifier from its unit/measurement (including parenthetic equivalents), producing broken or contradictory numeric claims when pieces are translated separately.

The prompt underrates clause‑initial function words: it often cuts between a single-word clause starter (determiner/pronoun) and the content word that immediately follows, detaching the head or predicate and breaking predicate-argument or noun‑head coherence.

diagnosis.why: The new fallback that prioritizes keeping numerals adjacent to their units made the model avoid punctuation/clause-boundary cuts and instead pick earlier internal cuts; that fixed many short/numeric splits (positive mean change in the ≤3/≤5/≤7 bins) but degraded performance on longer pieces where demoting punctuation boundaries produced awkward internal splits (negative mean change in the ≤10 and ≤99 bins and nearly equal n_worse/n_better).
diagnosis.lesson: Later revisions should protect numeral+unit adjacency but not demote punctuation/clause-boundary cuts across the board — keep punctuation boundaries as the fallback for longer segments or when no numeral/unit candidate is present.
